The same value is passed as a channel index to the script-request search 0x003DC050, so wait slot i and resource channel i are one index space. The bind 0x0026C8C0 does not write it: its rdi is an ActorManagerSlot, not this record.

name: partySlot
meaning: The record's own active party slot, 0..3, with 0xFF for unassigned: the index into PartyRosterSlots at 0x0209A1F0. It is signed, and the sign rejects the sentinel.

name: flags13
meaning: masked to the bits under mask `0x3C` only (&0x3C)

name: flags14
meaning: bit 0x80 cleared (&0x7F) at entry, then rewritten

name: handleTag4
meaning: The index of the owning ActorManagerSlot; the name handleTag4 is a key only, and the field is the owner slot index, not a tag. Writer: the record initialiser 0x00266530 takes the manager slot in rcx and moves it to r14 at 0x00266561; at 0x00266616 it loads movzx eax, byte [r14+0x28] (ActorManagerSlot +0x028 slotIndex) and at 0x00266624 stores mov byte [rbx+0x15], al, with rbx the record, so the record is stamped with its owner's index when it is initialised. Encoder: 0x0046BE80 packs (((w[+0x16] & 0x7FF) << 4) or (b[+0x15] & 0xF)) << 16, or-ed with w[+0x00], placing this field in the handle bits 0xF0000. Decoder: the handle resolver 0x003588B0 extracts those bits with shr eax,0x10 / and eax,0xf (0x3588D0/0x3588D9), rejects eax >= 5 at 0x3588DF, and hands the result to 0x00263FF0, whose whole body is movsxd rax,ecx / lea rcx,[0x2098E10] / imul rax,rax,0x288 / add rax,rcx: the ActorManagerSlot array at 0x02098E10, stride 0x288, count 5, a count the decoder's >= 5 bound reproduces. 0x00266624 is the writer shown to reach this record; byte writes to [reg+0x15] occur at 58 sites in about thirty functions across the image, and no other of them is shown to reach it. The decoder has been executed in a native replay; the writer and encoder are static reads.

name: handleTag11
meaning: The actor handle's 11-bit high field: 0x003589B0 reads a word and masks 0x7FF. 0x002659D0 advances it on re-install with a period of 2047: the value cycles 1..0x7FF and is never 0, so a handle repeats after 2047 advances of the same record. The handle resolver 0x003588B0, executed in a native replay, extracts (handle >> 20) & 0x7FF with shr edi,0x14 / and edi,0x7ff (0x3588CD/0x3588D3), resolves the record and finishes with movzx ecx, word [rax+0x16] / cmp ecx,edi / cmovne rax, 0 (0x358913-0x358925), so a handle whose tag no longer matches the record's resolves to null rather than to the wrong actor. A stale handle therefore reads as no actor, not as a crash; but a handle presented again after 2047 advances matches the record again, so BattleUnit.actorHandle is not stable across slot reuse and no handle is permanently unique.

name: pairLinkState
meaning: pair-link state: 0 = unlinked, 1 = the linked side, 2 = the side that initiated the link; the partner is named by +0x19 (its manager slot) and +0x1A (its id word). The multi-actor submitter skips targets whose state is 1

name: pairPartnerSlot
meaning: the pair partner's manager slot (copied from the partner's +0x15); read signed to index the slot array 0x02098E10 at stride 0x288

name: pairPartnerId
meaning: the pair partner's id word (copied from the partner's +0x00); 0xFFFF when unlinked (the 0xFFFF0000 dword init at 0x00269500)

name: flags1C
meaning: A dword of flags. From every recorded mask plus the initialiser's six writes: bit 0x4 is set by 0x00266A3A or dword 4 on the kind-3 path and cleared by 0x00266A4E and two other recorded sites; bit 0x100 is cleared; bit 0x400 is set twice and cleared twice (0x0025AF07, 0x0025AF22, 0x0025B943, 0x00268DAC), and on the kind-3 path the initialiser sets it at 0x00266A89 or clears it at 0x00266AA4; bit 0x2000 is cleared, and bits 0x100 and 0x2000 are cleared together by 0x002666F1 and dword 0xFFFFDEFF on the kind-3 path. Bits 0x8, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x800, 0x10000 and 0x20000 are tested, at 0x0025C47D, 0x0025C780/0x0025D30E, 0x0025C717/0x0025D24F, 0x0025B2A6, 0x0025E12B, 0x0025BCC3/0x00268F2B and 0x00268EDC; 0x0025C830 also tests bit 0x8 at 0x0025CF8C, bit 0x100 at 0x0025D103 and bit 0x2000 at 0x0025D03E; the recorded accesses do not cover this type's writers and include no writer of them. Bits 0x1, 0x2, 0x80, 0x200, 0x1000, 0x4000, 0x8000 and 0x40000 and above are touched by no mask; six further accesses read or test the whole dword without an immediate. The script verbs reqenable (002A), setupbattle (0056) and fieldsign (0176) each or in 1 << argBit through 0x0026B4A0: field-sign uses bit 0x100 and the runtime refresh bit 0x400. The initialiser's writes are kind-3 only: 0x002666BB movzx eax, byte ptr [rbx+3] / and al,0xE0 / 0x002666ED cmp al,0x60 guards 0x002666F1 and dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 0xFFFFDEFF, and a second gate at 0x002669FA-0x00266A02 guards the other five: either 0x00266A3A or dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 4 or 0x00266A4E and dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 0xFFFFFFFB, and then either 0x00266A89 or dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 0x400 followed by 0x00266A9E and dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 0xFFFFFFFB, or 0x00266AA4 and dword ptr [rbx+0x1C], 0xFFFFFBFF. On a record that is not kind 3 the initialiser never touches bits 0x4, 0x100, 0x400 or 0x2000, so they hold what the carve left; the descriptor table pairs kind 3 with sequences 5, 6 and 7 only, so the five small shapes never get these bits initialised.

name: initByte20
meaning: A byte written from cl by the initialiser.

name: initWord21
meaning: A word zeroed by the initialiser.

name: boundBlockBits
meaning: Bits that 0x0037B4D0 sets on the record bound to the binding block it is handed (the record it decodes with 0x0020E600 from the block's +0x0 at 0x0037B522): bit 0x1 at 0x0037B701, bit 0x2 at 0x0037B962, bit 0x4 at 0x0037BA5D, and bit 0x8 << the block's byte +0xA at 0x0037BB69-0x0037BB74. Each bind clears the byte: 0x0037CE80 (0x0037CEE3) and 0x0037CF50 (0x0037CFA2) zero it on the record whose 32-bit offset they store at the block's +0x0, and 0x0037C1A0 (0x0037C254) and 0x0037C730 (0x0037C806) on the roster record whose offset they store in their static block before they call 0x0037B4D0. Every access to this byte through the record is one of these nine, and the read at 0x0037BB69 only feeds the bit set at 0x0037BB74. Zero from the records block's memset at allocation (0x00861EC0 at 0x00267A8B).

name: requestAllChannelMask
meaning: 1 << channel for each channel on which this actor issued a counted multi-actor request (the `REQIALL` path that increments +0x10); cleared per channel with +0x06 and +0x26 when that channel's list empties.

name: submittedChannelMask
meaning: 1 << channel for each channel on which this actor has a successful submit - every single-actor submit, and multi-actor submits while +0x10 is non-zero; cleared per channel with +0x06 and +0x24

name: initDword28
meaning: A dword zeroed by the initialiser, whose qword store 0x00266603 mov qword ptr [rbx+0x28], r13 also covers +0x2C; the field is declared 4 bytes. The store 0x0026C957 mov dword ptr [rdi+0x28], ebp is the bind 0x0026C8C0's write of ActorManagerSlot +0x28, not of this record.

name: pad2C
meaning: Alignment after the +0x28 bytes, written only as the high half of the initialiser's qword store at +0x28 (0x00266603 mov qword [rbx+0x28], r13) and read by no instruction. None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. Zero from the records block's memset at allocation (0x00861EC0 at 0x00267A8B) and untouched after.

name: battleUnit
meaning: A non-owning back-pointer to this actor's BattleUnit pool slot, or null when it has no combat slot. The slot belongs to the pool and is reclaimed by index, not through this pointer. The bind 0x0026C8C0 does not write it: its rdi is an ActorManagerSlot, not this record.

name: boundBattleUnitPtr38
meaning: The bound battle-unit pointer: zeroed by the initialiser, stored at 0x00265AA8 by the battle-unit binder and read at 0x0025E20E by the actor runtime update.

name: actorImageEntry
meaning: A pointer to the actor's own authored entry inside the loaded script image's entry table: 0x30 bytes, and the three pointers below are all built from fields of this entry. The entry's +0x06 is a party code, its +0x08 the bytecode offset, its +0x10 and +0x14 two table offsets, its +0x1C a local-variable area offset.

name: scriptFunctionOffsetTable
meaning: The actor's function-offset table: image base + the resolved offset at entry+0x10. Indexed at an 8-byte stride by the bytecode-offset getter 0x00358A00, and a script's entry point is scriptBytecodeBase + this table's entry for the function id.

name: payloadSectionA
meaning: Image base + the resolved offset at entry+0x14, a second per-actor table. 0x003589E0 indexes it at a 4-byte stride; that one consumer fixes the element width and does not show what the elements hold, so the name stays generic.

name: scriptBytecodeBase
meaning: The actor's bytecode base: image base + the raw dword at entry+0x08. A script's program counter is this plus the function table's offset for the id. It is a different kind of value from +0x50.

name: entryFreeListHead
meaning: Head index of the ActorResourceEntry free list; 0xFF when the pool is exhausted. A removed entry is pushed here by the byte store at 0x003DB3F9 mov byte ptr [rbx + 0x60], sil. The bind 0x0026C8C0 writes a qword at 0x0026CB38 mov qword ptr [rdi + 0x60], rax, but its rdi is an ActorManagerSlot, and the value is the static 0x02099FF0 (lea at 0x0026CB31), not 0x0209A1F0; no qword read of this offset exists in the 1147 actor-owned bodies, so the field is the byte.

name: detachedEntryListHead
meaning: Head index of the list holding entries whose state byte (+0x10) is 4, entries that are not chained on any channel. 0xFF when empty.

name: selectedEntryIndex
meaning: An ActorResourceEntry ordinal the actor update pass resolves through the entry getter 0x003DB550; 0xFF is the null ordinal. It sits in the +0x60..+0x63 cluster with the free-list head, the detached-list head and the list flags.

name: entryListFlags
meaning: Bit `0x2` is set whenever an entry is returned to the free list.

name: vmRegI0

None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. name: slotCountA8
meaning: element count of the +0xA8 array: 8, or 6 when the kind table sub byte (0x01E0C329 + seq*4) is 1

name: slotCountA0
meaning: element count of the +0xA0 array: 10, or 8 when the kind table sub byte is 1

name: pad8A
meaning: Alignment between entryCount +0x89 and channelTail +0x8C. None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. name: channelTail
meaning: Per-channel tail entry index, one byte per channel, 0xFF when the channel list is empty. Only the first slotCountA8 bytes are used: 8 bytes is the maximum extent, not the used extent.

name: channelHead
meaning: Per-channel head entry index, one byte per channel, 0xFF when the channel list is empty. Only the first slotCountA8 bytes are used.

name: pad9C

None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. name: slotsA0

name: slotsA8
meaning: An interior pointer into this same record: the base of slotCountA8 elements of stride 0x28, the record tail on all eight per-kind sizes. The initialiser clears each element's prefix (qword +0, qword +8, dword +0x10, word +0x14, byte +0x16), so +0x18..+0x27 are not cleared at construction. name: padB0
meaning: The qword between waitSlots +0xA8 and movementContext +0xB8. None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. Zero from the records block's memset at allocation (0x00861EC0 at 0x00267A8B) and untouched after.

name: contextPtr

Read, not written, at 0x002665CE; the steering-mode setter 0x0026AE90 reads its actor's +0xB8 as the movement context.

name: secondaryContextPtr

name: overrideSlots

A reader takes slot k, or on 0xFFFF element k of the authored entry's count-prefixed list reached through +0x18 (0x002652D0 bounded to 0x11; 0x00269860 slots 7 and 14; fixed slots such as 0x0025C490). The script VM writes a slot by index through 0x0025AF60 (0x0025AFA1 mov word [rax + rbx*2 + 0xC8], di). Override slot k selects footer word k, special type k (the footer counted from 0).

name: initDwordEC

name: pad11C

None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here, and no block copy covers the record. This is the kind 3, sequence 5 and 6 layout, the 0x6E0 size of the type row. The extent depends on the sequence: the planter runs this region from +0x120 to wherever that sequence's arm places slotsA0. Sequence 0 has no movement context (+0xB8 is stored null and the resource pool starts at +0x120); sequences 1 and 2 get 0x80, sequences 3 and 4 get 0x20, and only sequences 5, 6 and 7 get the full 0x230 that every MovementContext field needs. name: secondaryContext

The other six per-kind sizes place the same regions at different offsets (the region table in the record page, section 12), so a reader resolving a field in this range must branch on rec[3] & 0x1F, not on this field alone.

name: resourceEntryPool

This is the kind 3, sequence 5 and 6 layout, the 0x6E0 size of the type row. The other six per-kind sizes place the same regions at different offsets (the region table in the record page, section 12), so a reader resolving a field in this range must branch on rec[3] & 0x1F, not on this field alone.

name: waitSlotArray

This is the kind 3, sequence 5 and 6 layout, the 0x6E0 size of the type row. The other six per-kind sizes place the same regions at different offsets (the region table in the record page, section 12), so a reader resolving a field in this range must branch on rec[3] & 0x1F, not on this field alone.

name: readyA

name: readyB

name: instructionPointerOrWaitKey

name: nativeTargetOrdinal
meaning: Saved target ordinal of the native `CALL` variants: selected on phase 0 and consumed by the lifecycle lookup on each invocation; not a stable actor-allocation identity. This is its use by the native `CALL` request kinds.

name: value

name: accumulator
meaning: Interpreter request accumulator: written and read by `POPA` / `PUSHA` and by the `CALL*POPA` result handling; it persists across interpreter entries. This is its use on the tested execution paths.

name: waitKind
meaning: Driver dispatch:0 or >=8 parks without interpreter;1/2 execute;3 waits for matching entry absence;4 waits for a matching detached continuation notification;5 scans actor/entry list;6 waits for a channel bit to clear;7 scans actor/channel list. Completion sets1 and can run bytecode within the same invocation.

name: commandPhase
meaning: Native lifecycle phase on the same ActorWaitSlot: 0 begin pending, 1 poll pending, 2 int and 3 or more float typing during completion. Busy writes 1; completion resets it to 0. Result callbacks can select 2 or 3 transiently. This byte is not the target's ActorStorageRecord +15 or the runtime indexed byte 0x02099011 + idx*288.

name: parked

name: pad17

No recorded access to the slots (the +0xA8 chain, 120 functions) falls here: the +0x16 word access listed there (0x003589B5) is 0x003589B0's read of the actor record's discriminator word, not a wait slot. None of the 279 recorded accesses to the record (by 120 functions, through the pool pointer and the +0xA0 / +0xA8 chains) falls here either, and no block copy covers it. Zero from the records block's memset at allocation (0x00861EC0 at 0x00267A8B) and untouched after.

name: targetRef
meaning: A base-relative reference to another actor record, not a pointer and not a handle: 0x0020E600 resolves it as arg + *(0x01F83530). Wait kinds 3 and 6 resolve it to get the actor they wait on; kinds 5 and 7 pass the address &slot[0x18] as a descriptor. Execution-kind native commands use slot +0x18 as scratch instead: wait stores a signed countdown here, and the begin and poll paths keep a scratch pointer here (0x002621D0; 0x0034CF90 / 0x0034DCC0). So the value is an encoded actor reference only for the wait kinds.

name: waitListRef
meaning: For wait kinds5/7, encoded list reference read by002674B0/0x00267420 from descriptor+4, resolved by0020E600. List starts with DWORD count followed by four-byte actor/ID pairs (ID ignored for channel wait). Other command-scratch uses overlap these bytes.

name: waitResourceId
meaning: The resource id wait kind 3 matches against the target actor's entries, through the active-entry search 0x003DBF60.

name: waitListCursor
meaning: For wait kinds 5 and 7, the retained forward cursor: the helpers increment it past satisfied entries and stop on the first active entry, so later polls begin here rather than rescanning earlier actors. Its other uses are kind-dependent scratch. Slot +0x18..+0x27 doubles as the native-command scratch window: the command lifecycle forms r8 = slot + 0x18 and reads dword r8+0xC (+0x24) and qword r8+8 (+0x20), so a native command can overwrite an armed wait's bytes before any read.

name: targetOrdinal
meaning: The ordinal of the actor this wait was armed against, saved so the resuming opcode can register again without deriving it; it is the ordinal the ordinal getter 0x00358940 takes, distinct from targetRef +0x18, the base-relative reference to the record. Slot +0x18..+0x27 doubles as the native-command scratch window: the command lifecycle forms r8 = slot + 0x18 and reads dword r8+0xC (+0x24) and qword r8+8 (+0x20), so a native command can overwrite an armed wait's bytes before any read.

name: waitChannel
meaning: The resource channel that wait kind 6 tests on the target actor, through the channel-bit test 0x003DB640. Slot +0x18..+0x27 doubles as the native-command scratch window: the command lifecycle forms r8 = slot + 0x18 and reads dword r8+0xC (+0x24) and qword r8+8 (+0x20), so a native command can overwrite an armed wait's bytes before any read.

name: settled
meaning: Set to 1 on completed kind 3, 6 and 7 waits; kind 4 notification consumption and kind 5 list completion do not write it, so it is not a general completed-wait flag. Opcode 32 clears it when it arms kind 3. No instruction reads it as a settled flag: the interpreter clears it when it arms the next wait, and the next native command overwrites it first, since +0x18..+0x27 doubles as the native-command scratch window (r8 = slot+0x18; dword r8+0xC = +0x24, qword r8+8 = +0x20).

name: subgroupCounts
meaning: The per-subgroup order counts, one byte each. The gambit walk sums them to find where a subgroup's orders begin: it steps two at a time into two accumulators (0x00305D30/0x00305D37, add rcx, 2) for indices below subgroupIndex-1, adds the odd leftover byte at 0x00305D4E, and uses the total as the index into the record array. The subgroup's own count byte is then tested against zero at 0x00305D89 and an empty subgroup walks nothing.

name: orders
meaning: Room for fourteen runtime order records of 0x18, +0x20..+0x16F (0x170 = 0x20 + 14 x 0x18, the set stride: 0x00328160 imul r13, rax, 0x170). The three rebuilders 0x00328140, 0x00327DE0 and 0x00327F80 each make twelve passes (0x00328187 / 0x00327E1A / 0x00327FF4 lea r15d, [r12 + 0xc]; one record at most per pass), so at most twelve records are filled and records 12 and 13 (+0x140..+0x16F) keep their zero from load (.bss at 0x02089378). The one stride-indexed reader, the gambit walk 0x00305CC0 (set from BattleUnit +0x6E0, stored at 0x0023AB9F), reads record sum(subgroupCounts below the subgroup) + j for j below the subgroup's count (0x00305D30..0x00305D97). The rebuilders write the count byte +0x000 (0x003282A0 / 0x00327F60 / 0x0032810B), at most 12, so the walk stays below +0x140. No fixed displacement reaches +0x140..+0x16F (5 base formations in 4 bodies; 0 image-base-relative). A config line that is disabled or empty never becomes a record here, so the evaluator never sees it.

name: free

name: ambienceVoice

name: crossFadeCounter

name: ambienceId
meaning: the current ambience id: the selection 0x00363B40 makes from the weather selections; handed to 0x00363840 when +0xBD is set

name: appliedListenerValue
meaning: the value last applied through 0x002DF410 by the listener update 0x00362850: it recomputes a value, replaces it with +0x14 while +0x21 is set, and calls 0x002DF410 only when it differs from this.

name: forcedListenerValue
meaning: the override for +0x10 while +0x21 is set; written with +0x21 by 0x003631A0

name: boundHandle
meaning: the third argument 0x003635E0 stores when it binds a map sound list; 0x00363750 hands it to 0x002DEB40 when it is not negative and then stores -1 (the reset does not write it)

name: listenerHeading
meaning: the listener's heading: written by the listener update from its atan2 result (normalised by 0x003A1C50), or copied from the microphone heading +0x3C while microphone mode +0x2A is set; read by the spatial-audio frame

name: sourceWalkEnabled
meaning: set by the one-byte setter 0x00363A80 (cl); cleared when a source table is published (0x003635C0) or dropped (0x00363730, 0x00363750) and by the reset; the listener update resolves the source records in +0x80 only while it is non-zero. The name is from that gate.

name: forceListenerValue
meaning: 1 while +0x14 overrides +0x10; set with +0x14 by 0x003631A0

name: ambienceVolume
meaning: the ambience target volume (0x7F at reset): passed to 0x002DEF40 when the ambience starts, and applied to the playing voice through 0x002DF150 by the per-frame step whenever it differs from +0x23

name: appliedAmbienceVolume
meaning: the volume last applied to the playing ambience (copy of +0x22 at each start and after each 0x002DF150 change)

name: mapSoundVolume
meaning: the map sound volume, 0-127, that character and effect sounds take: the template copies give it to a request's byte +0x19 (0x00361750 at 0x0036175F, 0x003617B0 at 0x003617B7), the point-sound steps 0x00361BF0 (0x00361CB2) and 0x00361CF0 (0x00361DAF) scale their volume by it / 127, and the map-sound start 0x003638B0 reads it (0x00363946, 0x003639B4). 0x00362D20 moves it each pass to start x (1 - progress) + target x progress (+0x28, +0x29, +0x30; 0x00362D98); 0x003634B0(frames, volume) starts that fade from its current value (0x003634EF) or sets it at once (0x00363549); 0x7F from 0x00362C60 (0x00362CBA), the reset 0x00362F70 (0x00363007), the bind 0x003635E0 (0x0036368C), 0x00363B40 (0x00363D75, 0x00363E08) and 0x00363E40 (0x00363ECF, 0x00363F1F).

Read only by 0x00362D20 (0x00362D68).

name: microphoneMode

name: spatialSourceTable

name: mapSoundList

name: listenerPosition

name: microphonePosition

name: movingSoundRange

The constructor 0x001A1420 stores only +0x0, +0x8 and +0x10 (0x001A143B, 0x001A143E, 0x001A144A), so +0x18 holds no constructor value. The per-frame pump 0x0017D6E0 loads this object from 0x01F7F4C0 at 0x0017D748 and checkpoints it at 0x0017D757, which dominates its conditional teardown call at 0x0017D83F; the teardown 0x001E0590 reloads 0x01F7F4C0 at 0x001E05C0 and rolls back at 0x001E05C7. name: queryDefault58

name: pokeGate70

name: opaquePosted

name: mapOpaquePosted

name: charsWithOpaque

name: pad7F
meaning: Alignment fill before the lock at +0x80; no instruction addresses it. Lifetime: zero from the loader (image 0x01F7F490 past the .data raw end).

name: platformLock
meaning: an embedded 0x28-byte recursive lock (init byte +0x0, event handle +0x8, byte +0x10, waiter count +0x18, owner thread +0x20, recursion depth +0x24): 0x0015BCD0 constructs it with 0x005CC8A0 and registers the teardown 0x008A6990; 0x0017ED20 creates its event on first use (0x005CD0A0 -> CreateEventA) and locks it (0x005CD370 -> 0x005CD380); 0x0017F760 unlocks it (0x005CD7D0)

name: pokeStatusA8

name: parkedCubemapIntensity

name: pokeGate70Once
meaning: once-flag for arming +0x70: 0x00184740 arms +0x70 only while this is 0 and sets it to 1 in the same step; 0x00182D30 clears it

name: padB4
meaning: Fill to the 16-byte boundary at +0xC0; no instruction addresses it, and the code does not show that the run there needs 16-byte alignment. Lifetime: zero from the loader (image 0x01F7F490 past the .data raw end).

name: flareMatrix
meaning: 0x01F7F550: the lens-flare pass's corner matrix: 0x0017ED50 multiplies each row of the matrix it is given by the render manager's matrix +0x6C8 (0x0017E7E0 at 0x0017EDE4-0x0017EE20) and stores the four rows here (0x0017EE41-0x0017EF01), returning this address (0x0017EE3A); its only caller 0x00376470 transforms the flare's corners by it (0x00202D70 at 0x00376843-0x00376850; Lens flares)

name: blockBankIndex
meaning: A bank index in 0..3: 0x00185A50 and the render pass 0x00187950 pass it as r8d and then store (index + 1) and 3; the render-block and save-image Platform bodies pass the current value as their bank argument (r8d).

name: aoRanLatch
meaning: set to 1 by AmbientOcclusionObj::Execute 0x001F28B0 only on the path where AO ran; zeroed by the render pass 0x00187950 before the part-0 walk when render params +0x199 is set; while 0x01DF08FC is 0 and this is non-zero, the forward walk 0x0018B100 exits at the next entry that passes the mask (I-7)

name: pad105
meaning: Alignment fill before the pointer at +0x108; no instruction addresses it. Lifetime: zero from the loader (image 0x01F7F490 past the .data raw end).

name: perFrameSingletonCell
meaning: The pointer to the 0xDD8 per-frame singleton (BootSingleton01F7F598): Ensure 0x00189000 allocates and constructs it (0x00184F20) when it is null and stores it; 0x00189120 is the getter; the camera publish's bank parity is that object's +0x1C.

name: renderPassCounter
meaning: incremented once at the end of each render pass 0x00187950; its readers take it modulo a count to pick a slot (0x0017E8E0 divides it by r15d and uses the remainder)

name: areaEntryCounter
meaning: The area-entry counter that feeds the `LCG` seed. Both of its references are 4-byte and both are in one function, 0x002342F0: a read at 0x00234301 (`mov eax, dword ptr [0x0208E6B0]`) and a write at 0x00234315 (`mov dword ptr [0x0208E6B0], eax`) - a read-modify-write bump with no other toucher anywhere in the image. It is in .bss, so it starts at zero.

name: handleA
meaning: bank handle A, the one both documented wrappers use (0x003A1180 at 0x003A119C, 0x003A11F0); 0x003A1390 stores it (0x003A13A4), and the start-up loader 0x003A13F0 stores -1 in it before requesting blocks 0 and 1 (0x003A14BE, 0x003A153D)

name: handleB
meaning: bank handle B; its readers treat -1 as no handle (0x003A1076, 0x003A1106); the teardown never writes it

name: handleC
meaning: bank handle C: 0x003A12D0 stores it (0x003A12E4) and 0x003A1070 reads it (0x003A1095); the start-up loader 0x003A13F0 stores -1 in it before requesting block 2 (0x003A15BC)

name: nextSlotLink
meaning: The list link, signed. 0x003A0C90 reads it with `movsx r8d, word ptr [base + slot*24 + 0]` and terminates the walk on a negative value (`jns` continues), so the list is null-terminated by sign rather than by a sentinel index. The walk starts from the head word at 0x02AEF3C0 and treats 0x40 (64, one past the last slot) as the end of the list.

name: previousSlotLink
meaning: the previous link, signed int16: set to r-1 by 0x003A13F0 (0x003A144E), to 65 by 0x003A0F80 (0x003A1039) and to the predecessor's index by 0x003A0C90 (0x003A0D96); 0x003A1750 reads it (0x003A175C) to relink the neighbour (0x003A17AE) and writes -1 (0x003A17B9)

name: matchId
meaning: the value the list walk compares its search key against: 0x003A0CC7 `cmp esi, dword ptr [base + slot*24 + 4]`. Width from the access instruction.

name: keyLow
meaning: The low half of a 32-bit key stored as two words, not an independent field. 0x003A1240 does `movzx r9d, word [+8]` then `movzx r8d, word [+0xa]`, `shl r8d, 0x10`, `or r8d, r9d` - assembling one dword with the high half at +0x0A - and compares it against the caller's id with bit 0x80000000 cleared (`btr ecx, 0x1f`). The low half is then `shl r9d, 9` (x512) and added to the caller's base, which is where the 64*512 id space comes from. The `test r9d,r9d / js` that follows never jumps: r9d is a movzx of a word and cannot be negative.

name: keyHigh
meaning: the high half of the 32-bit key assembled at 0x003A1264 (`shl r8d, 0x10`). Paired with +0x08; see that field.

name: stateByte000C
meaning: A state byte: 0x003A0F18 stores 2 (mov byte [rdi+0xC], 2) and 0x003A12C5 reads it (movzx eax, byte [r8+0xC]). The acquire 0x003A0C90 stores qword 0x10000 at +0x0C of a fresh slot (0x003A0DBB), so +0x0C, +0x0D and +0x10 start at 0 and +0x0E at 1. The 64 slots of 0x18 at 0x02AEEDC0 are addressed through rip-relative leas of 0x02AEEDC0 and through the image base (the acquire 0x003A0C90 forms the slot base as r14 + 0x29cedc0, r14 the image base); following the rip-relative leas gives 50 accesses at 10 offsets in 13 bodies. 0x003A0EA0 forms slot i with lea r12, [0x02AEEDC0] (0x003A0EC9) and r12 + i x 24 (0x003A0EFA-0x003A0EFE), 0x003A0F80 does the same at 0x003A0FA8, and the same base stores the free marker -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to matchId +0x04 (0x003A0FFD); 0x003A0EA0 also walks the bitmap 0x02AEF3F0 beside the slots.

name: flagByte000D
meaning: A one-bit condition: 0x003A1318, 0x003A1378 and 0x003A13D8 each store 1 (mov byte [r8+0xD], 1), and 0x003A0FDC tests it (cmp byte [rbx+0xD], dil, against a register that is zero on that path). The acquire 0x003A0C90 stores qword 0x10000 at +0x0C of a fresh slot (0x003A0DBB), so +0x0C, +0x0D and +0x10 start at 0 and +0x0E at 1. The 64 slots of 0x18 at 0x02AEEDC0 are addressed through rip-relative leas of 0x02AEEDC0 and through the image base (the acquire 0x003A0C90 forms the slot base as r14 + 0x29cedc0, r14 the image base); following the rip-relative leas gives 50 accesses at 10 offsets in 13 bodies. 0x003A0EA0 forms slot i with lea r12, [0x02AEEDC0] (0x003A0EC9) and r12 + i x 24 (0x003A0EFA-0x003A0EFE), 0x003A0F80 does the same at 0x003A0FA8, and the same base stores the free marker -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to matchId +0x04 (0x003A0FFD); 0x003A0EA0 also walks the bitmap 0x02AEF3F0 beside the slots.

name: counter000E
meaning: The slot's reference count. The acquire 0x003A0C90 looks the id up among the live slots and, when slot +0x04 matches, adds 1 (inc word ptr [rbx+0xE] at 0x003A0D0E) and returns the slot's handle; a fresh slot starts at 1 (qword 0x10000 at +0x0C, 0x003A0DBB). The release path decrements it (0x003A0FE2 dec word ptr [rbx+0xE]) and compares it with zero (0x003A0FE6 cmp word ptr [rbx+0xE], di), and stamps matchId with -1 four instructions later. The 64 slots of 0x18 at 0x02AEEDC0 are addressed through rip-relative leas of 0x02AEEDC0 and through the image base (the acquire 0x003A0C90 forms the slot base as r14 + 0x29cedc0, r14 the image base); following the rip-relative leas gives 50 accesses at 10 offsets in 13 bodies. 0x003A0EA0 forms slot i with lea r12, [0x02AEEDC0] (0x003A0EC9) and r12 + i x 24 (0x003A0EFA-0x003A0EFE), 0x003A0F80 does the same at 0x003A0FA8, and the same base stores the free marker -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to matchId +0x04 (0x003A0FFD); 0x003A0EA0 also walks the bitmap 0x02AEF3F0 beside the slots.

name: handleDword0010
meaning: A non-zero-when-live identifier handed to another subsystem: 0x003A0F02 loads it (mov ecx, [rdi+0x10]) and the slot is skipped when it is zero (test ecx, ecx / je); 0x003A0F09 calls 0x002DEE90 with it in ecx; 0x003A0F23 clears it on release (mov dword [rdi+0x10], r15d with r15d zero). The acquire 0x003A0C90 stores qword 0x10000 at +0x0C of a fresh slot (0x003A0DBB), so +0x0C, +0x0D and +0x10 start at 0 and +0x0E at 1. The 64 slots of 0x18 at 0x02AEEDC0 are addressed through rip-relative leas of 0x02AEEDC0 and through the image base (the acquire 0x003A0C90 forms the slot base as r14 + 0x29cedc0, r14 the image base); following the rip-relative leas gives 50 accesses at 10 offsets in 13 bodies. 0x003A0EA0 forms slot i with lea r12, [0x02AEEDC0] (0x003A0EC9) and r12 + i x 24 (0x003A0EFA-0x003A0EFE), 0x003A0F80 does the same at 0x003A0FA8, and the same base stores the free marker -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to matchId +0x04 (0x003A0FFD); 0x003A0EA0 also walks the bitmap 0x02AEF3F0 beside the slots.

name: handleDword0014
meaning: A second identifier on the same release path, handed to a different callee than +0x10: read into ecx twice (0x003A0F33 and 0x003A0F3B, each followed by a call to 0x0036D200) and cleared with zero at 0x003A0F43. The 64 slots of 0x18 at 0x02AEEDC0 are addressed through rip-relative leas of 0x02AEEDC0 and through the image base (the acquire 0x003A0C90 forms the slot base as r14 + 0x29cedc0, r14 the image base); following the rip-relative leas gives 50 accesses at 10 offsets in 13 bodies. 0x003A0EA0 forms slot i with lea r12, [0x02AEEDC0] (0x003A0EC9) and r12 + i x 24 (0x003A0EFA-0x003A0EFE), 0x003A0F80 does the same at 0x003A0FA8, and the same base stores the free marker -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to matchId +0x04 (0x003A0FFD); 0x003A0EA0 also walks the bitmap 0x02AEF3F0 beside the slots.

name: headSlotIndex
meaning: index of the first AudioBankSlot in the list, negative = empty

name: vtable
meaning: a vtable pointer installed into every element by the initialiser loop

name: start
meaning: The value the ramp interpolates from.

name: target
meaning: the value it interpolates TO, and the value returned outright when duration == 0

name: elapsed
meaning: Numerator of the normalised progress; no reader clamps it (0x007A9E00 divides it by duration at 0x007A9E21-0x007A9E29), but the advancer 0x007AA770 adds the step and stores duration in it once it reaches duration, clearing the active byte +0x20 (0x007AA7D4-0x007AA7EE, 0x007AA834-0x007AA84E), so the progress tops out at 1.0.

name: duration
meaning: Denominator; exactly 0.0 means snap to target, tested by equality, not by a threshold.

name: pad18
meaning: moved only as a dword by the sound copy 0x007BFFA0 (e.g. 0x007BFFFA reads the +0x248 ramp's, 0x007C0000 writes it); read and written by no other function; nothing fixes its width

name: curve
meaning: 0..5 selects the fade shape. A value above 5 takes a separate exit at 0x007A9F14 that runs xorps xmm0, xmm0 first and returns 0; arm 0 is 0x007A9F17, one byte past it, and returns t unchanged (the linear fade).

name: activeFlag
meaning: the active flag - the walker processes an element only when this byte is set; the initialiser clears it

name: pad21
meaning: the bytes between active +0x20 and limited +0x24: read and written by no function; nothing fixes their width (the sound copy 0x007BFFA0 moves +0x20 as a byte and +0x24 as a qword and skips them; only the bus clear 0x007AC5E4 and the external-voice clear 0x007A497B cover them)

name: limited
meaning: 1: the ramp keeps to its rise and fall rates: 0x007CA560 raises the duration to at least the change over the rate (0x007CA5D2), and Sound 0x007BE0B0 does for its +0x3C8 ramp (0x007BE207). Set to 1 by Sound slot 10 0x007BE510 for +0x1B8/+0x1E8/+0x218 (0x007BE533), slot 11 0x007BEC70 for the curved +0x88 (0x007BEC9F) and the sound-header load 0x007BDDA0 for +0x248/+0x278 (0x007BDEB7); 0 from every builder (0x007AA1D2, 0x007AC611, 0x007B8DDC, 0x007BC9D2, 0x007E7B43, 0x007EF9D1, 0x007F3E0D) and from 0x007BE579-0x007BE585, 0x007BECBD, 0x007BDEC1, 0x007C0531, 0x007C055B-0x007C05A4; copied by 0x007BFFA0

name: riseRate
meaning: the most the value may rise per second while +0x24 is 1: a new target above the current value gets a duration of at least (target - current) / abs(riseRate) (0x007CA5F6; 0x007BE23A for Sound +0x3C8). 5.0 from Sound slot 10 0x007BE510 (0x007BE533) and slot 11 0x007BEC70 (0x007BEC9F); the sound-header entry's f32 +0x10 from 0x007BDDA0 (0x007BDEB7); copied by the sound copy 0x007BFFA0; written by no other function

name: fallRate
meaning: the most the value may fall per second while +0x24 is 1: a new target at or below the current value gets a duration of at least (current - target) / abs(fallRate) (0x007CA617; 0x007BE256 for Sound +0x3C8). 5.0 from Sound slot 10 0x007BE510 (0x007BE547, 0x007BE555, 0x007BE563) and slot 11 0x007BEC70 (0x007BECA7); the sound-header entry's f32 +0x14 from 0x007BDDA0 (0x007BDEBC); copied by the sound copy 0x007BFFA0; written by no other function

name: gate
meaning: non-zero abandons the request before any lookup (the three readers branch on it)

name: entryCount
meaning: the number of entries, read as a word. The walk processes entryCount+1 of them - the bound is inclusive - so this is one less than the number of entries actually touched.

name: pad02
meaning: the two bytes between the entry count word and the first entry: read by no instruction in the registrar 0x003845F0 (0x00384688 movzx r14d, word [rax] reads the count; the entries start at +4, 0x0038469B lea rbx, [rax+4]) or the recursive walk 0x003846F0 (0x00384727 movzx ebx, word [rax]; 0x00384746 lea rbx, [r9+4]), the only two functions that resolve the table (header +0x14 through 0x0020E600); authored bytes of the blob, left as the file holds them - the relocation adds the base to the entries only (0x003846B9, 0x00384780)

name: firstEntry
meaning: The first of the four-byte entries. Each is a reference that 0x003846F0 converts with 0x0020E620, stores back, then resolves and descends into, a reference to another block of the same counted shape; consecutive entries do not bound a range. The final entry is instead rebased in place at 0x003846B9 with no descent.

name: expressions
meaning: four authored expressions evaluated in order, producing the four components of one value

name: modeFlags
meaning: the bits under mask `0x3` select how the four expressions are evaluated; bit 0x4 selects whether the result is normalised. The bits under mask `0xF8` unobserved

name: pad041
meaning: The 15-byte tail after modeFlags inside the 0x50 block; no instruction accesses it.

name: operandAPayload
meaning: Operand A's payload, read as a dword at 0x00431505 when operandAKind is 1 and passed to 0x0020E600, so for kind 1 it is a pack offset, not a value. For kind 2 and above it is the curve evaluator's input, and for kind 0 no instruction reads it. The same four bytes mean different things by kind, so the row is named payload rather than value.

name: operandBPayload
meaning: Operand B's payload, with the same kind-dependent reading as operand A. Per invariant I1, an absent B (kind 0) means the expression is just A.

name: operandABound
meaning: A per-operand modulus word, indexed by the operand index: 0x004310D0 reads movzx eax, word ptr [rsi + rdi*2 + 8] with rdi 0 for operand A and 1 for B, so A's word is here and B's at +0x0A. 0x004310D8 tests it and takes the zero branch when it is zero; otherwise 0x004310E1 compares the caller's value with it and proceeds only when the value is greater (cmp ebx, r9d / jle), into the division at 0x004310E6-0x004310E8: idiv r9d at 0x004310E9, and 0x004310EC mov ebx, edx keeps the remainder. So when the word is non-zero and the value exceeds it, the value is reduced modulo it; otherwise the value passes through unchanged.

name: operandBBound
meaning: Operand B's modulus word, reached by the same rdi*2 + 8 indexing with rdi = 1 on the same code path as operand A's +0x08: the division at 0x004310E9 is idiv r9d and 0x004310EC mov ebx, edx keeps the remainder, so when this word is non-zero and the caller's value exceeds it, the value is reduced modulo it; otherwise the value passes through unchanged.

Three kinds: 0 absent, yielding zero; 1 an authored-data reference, resolved through 0x0020E600 with the value taken from +0x04 of the target; 2 or more the piecewise curve 0x00431080, called with the operand's index (0 for A) rather than its payload.

name: flags
meaning: The operator and the per-operand selectors. Bits 0x3 are operand A's two-bit selector and bits 0xC operand B's: the piecewise curve 0x00431080 reads the word twice, on the operand-A path (r8d zero) movzx ecx, word ptr [rsi + 0xe] at 0x004310B5 then jmp 4310CA over the shift, on the operand-B path the same read at 0x004310C3 followed by shr ecx, 2, both arriving at and ecx, 3 (0x004310CD). The selector has three cases: at 0x00431106 zero jumps to 0x004312CF, one falls into 0x0043111C, and 2 and 3 take 0x00431113 xor ecx, ecx / mov eax, ecx and return zero via 0x0043131C. Case one reads the operand's kind (0x0043111C movzx eax, byte ptr [rdi + rsi + 0xc], operandAKind or operandBKind by the same index); kinds 0, 1 and 2 go where case zero went (cmp al, 2 / jbe), and only kind 3 or above continues, carrying the kind in r15d. Bits 0xF0 are the operator, extracted by 0x00431350 as (word >> 4) & 0xF: 0 returns a with no draw; 1, 2, 3 and 4 draw once; 5 draws only when b != a, jumping into op 1's arm; above 5 returns a. The applier 0x003112F0 reads it (0x00311394 test 0x4000, 0x003114D2, 0x00311781); the resolver 0x00385F60 clears bits 0x10 to 0x80 (0x00386849 and 0xffffff0f)

name: unobservedTail0144
meaning: The record's last four bytes, zero from the caller's stack-frame zero fill and the constructor's bulk clear; no recorded access reaches them on their own.

name: stored
meaning: the value an action keeps between its first list and its committed resolve: Dark Matter and Soul Purge move the Knot of Rust bank [0x02EBF190]+0x5B0C into it and deal it (0x0038DA5D, 0x0038DA68); Traveler stores its damage (0x0038ECD5, 0x0038ECFF) and deals it again without a stored preview (0x0038ED17); Gil Toss stores the gil sum (0x00388E51), copies it to result +0x08 for the other targets (0x00388E60) and slot 147 shares it among the targets (0x0038EDD6); cleared by 0x00385680 (0x003857AB) and 0x00386C10 (0x00386C5B)

name: failed
meaning: one bit per target index (unit +0xEA9, or the record's type byte +4): a first-list run that ends failed sets the target's bit (0x00385A7F in 0x00385680), and the committed resolve 0x00385F60 then gives that target result kind 6 without running a slot (0x0038633F); cleared by 0x003857AB and 0x00386C5B

name: immune
meaning: one bit per target index: set when the first list ends immune (0x00385AC0); the committed resolve gives result kind 10 (0x003862FB); cleared by 0x003857AE and 0x00386C5E

name: unitBitset00C
meaning: as +0x04: 0x00387B97 'or [rbx+0xC], 1<<cl' in 0x00387B00, which by its symbol name marks a target-history bit; 0x002FA352 'bt' in 0x002FA290. The purpose rests on that function name alone

name: shadesAction
meaning: the action Shades of Black (0x9F) turns into: 0x00387A50 stores the random pick of 0x00387130 (0x00387ADE) when unit +0x714 is 0x9F; 0x00387090 returns it (0x0038710E); 0x00385680 and 0x00385F60 put it in place of 0x9F in 0x02AEDFD4 (0x00385801, 0x00385FF7); 0x00385680 keeps it over its clear (0x003857A3, 0x003857E1); cleared by 0x00386C10 (0x00386C62)

name: flags
meaning: bit 0x1 the stored preview (set 0x003857DD, cleared 0x00386402; read by Numerology 0x00389D24, Dark Matter 0x0038DA49, Traveler 0x0038EC3A); mask 0xE the first list's result +0x18 mask 0xE (0x00385AC3-0x00385AF2), copied into the committed result's +0x18 (0x003860DF-0x00386108); mask 0xF0 the combo count (0x00388660: 0x0038885D, 0x00388865, 0x0038886B); 0x00385680 reads it before its clear and keeps the high nibble when unit +0x6B7 is set (0x0038579C, 0x003857C6-0x003857D9)

name: clearedByte013
meaning: written only as part of 0x003857B2's dword clear of +0x10..+0x13 and 0x00386C10's qword clear; never read

name: periodicTickCounter
meaning: stage 5's per-unit tick counter: 0x00386860 points rbx at it in either bank (0x0208D494 at 0x00386885-0x00386890, 0x0208DE94 at 0x003868AD-0x003868B8), reads it (0x003869A2), stores it (0x003869E0, 0x00386A2C) and steps it (0x00386A27)

name: clearedWord016
meaning: written only as part of 0x00386C10's qword clear of +0x10..+0x17; never read

name: walkLeft
meaning: the walk distance left after the last MP step: 0x002F9400 compares the new distance with it (0x002F9474) and stores what is left (0x002F95A6); cleared by 0x00386C10 (0x00386C66)

name: circle
meaning: bit 0x1: the unit joins the circling formation once KO'd, set by 0x0033CB10 (0x0033CB60) when action-timeline event 2 or 6 reaches a KO'd unit (0x00325260 at 0x00325651); bit 0x2: it has reached its place, set within 0.1 of it (0x0033DA73); both read by the mode-2 movement 0x0033D890 (0x0033D953, 0x0033DA77); cleared by 0x00386C10 (0x00386C66)

name: unobservedSpan020
meaning: Zero at load: the storage is in the .data tail past the raw end 0x01F7E400, which the loader fills with zeros. Neither set of recorded accesses reaches these 32 bytes, and they lie outside 0x00386C10's 0x20-byte reset; the shl 6 stride gives the record's extent.

name: formatMagic
meaning: format magic 0x05071901, written at reset and checked before the block is used

name: stateFlags
meaning: 32-bit flags word; the bits under mask `0x7000` are projected into SaveImageHeader+0x57 by the save finaliser

name: statsRecords
meaning: The 40 per-combatant BattleStatsRecord slots, 0x1C8 each, running +0x008..+0x4748 (40 x 0x1C8 = 0x4740); the inventory temporary-state snapshot follows at +0x4748. The bounds-checked accessor 0x0031B770 rejects an index above 0x27 (0x0031B776), computes the element address into rdi (0x0031B77B-0x0031B790), then walks every live BattleUnit (count from 0x00236850, unit from 0x00236820) in the loop 0x0031B7A5-0x0031B7C3, comparing [unit+0x698] with rdi at 0x0031B7B1 and returning 0 when nothing matches. A kind-1 unit's +0x698 holds the SpawnKeep entry's +0x80 page, not an element of this array, so this accessor resolves a slot only to a kind-0 unit, and no index reaches an enemy through it.

name: inventoryTemporaryStateA
meaning: The item count words, one per item id 0x0000-0x003F, each split into its low 10 bits and its top 6 bits (read apart by 0x002FD8D0 at 0x002FD92B and 0x002FD917): the first region of descriptor record 0 (inventory class 5), 64 uint16 entries. The snapshot 0x0030FBE0 copies each word to the backup at +0x4F84 and asks 0x003008A0 for a count of 0 (absolute, channel 1; 0x0030FC7F), which the packed handler stores in the low 10 bits, not below the value of the top 6 bits (0x002FD2E9-0x002FD31A); the restore 0x0030FAA0 gives each saved word, whole and sign-extended (0x0030FAE7), to 0x003008A0 as a relative channel-1 change (0x0030FAF5): the handler adds it to the low 10 bits, raises a result below the value of the top 6 bits to that value and caps any other result at 99; the restore then zeroes the 0x83C bytes from +0x4F84 (0x0030FBB1-0x0030FBC7). The four arrays at +0x4748, +0x47C8, +0x4F84 and +0x5004 are two source/backup pairs of differently-sized regions that abut, not halves of one thing. Each pair's count comes from its own global, and four loops agree: the item snapshot 0x0030FC50-0x0030FC8C bounded by [0x01EEBCD0] = 0x40, the item restore 0x0030FAD0-0x0030FB02 by [0x01EEBCFC] = 0x40, the equipment snapshot by [0x01EEBD28] = 0x1A4, the equipment restore 0x0030FB20-0x0030FB55 by [0x01EEBD54] = 0x1A4. Stride 2 at every site, for example 0x0030FAE7 movsx edx, word ptr [rax + rcx*2 + 0x4f84]. The layout agrees with 64 for the items: +0x4748 + 0x80 is +0x47C8 and +0x4F84 + 0x80 is +0x5004. The globals are read at run time, so 0x40 and 0x1A4 are the shipped image's values.

meaning: The first regions of descriptor records 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12 (inventory classes 7, 8, 9, 11, 13 and 17), laid consecutively after those of descriptors 0 and 1: the 512 loot count words at +0x4B10 (low 10 bits and top 6 bits read apart by 0x002FD8D0), then the owned bits of magicks at +0x4F10 (6 words), technicks at +0x4F1C (2), gambits at +0x4F20 (16), key items and maps at +0x4F40 (32) and Quickenings, Espers and Second Board at +0x4F80 (2), ending at +0x4F84. meaning: The rest of the 0x83C-byte backup area after the backups of the item and equipment count words; the area is as long as the live first regions +0x4748 to +0x4F84. name: itemEverOwned
meaning: the items' ever-owned bits, one per item id 0x0000-0x003F (byte index >> 3, bit index & 7), region C of descriptor record 0 at 0x01EEBCC0: set by 0x002FD150 when an item's count rises (0x002FD323-0x002FD34B); read by 0x002FD150 (0x002FD344), the query 0x002FD970 (0x002FD9D7) and 0x00309B83 (0x00309BC8); zeroed with the block by 0x002370C0 (0x002370D3) and with the save image by 0x002EF5F0 (0x002EF603) and 0x002EF650 (0x002EF663); copied with the save image by 0x00229B40, 0x005844A0, 0x002EF570, 0x0057E310, 0x002EF690 and the file write 0x00866AD0, loaded by the file read 0x00866A00 (0x00866A4D) and copied back from image +0x2200 by 0x002EF4A0 (0x002EF4C4)

name: inventoryDerivedState
meaning: The second region of item class 7 (loot, descriptor 2, count 0x200): one byte per loot id. 0x0030B6A0 binds block + [0x01EEBD88] (the cell 0x01EEBCC0 + 2 * 0x58 + 0x18) = block + 0x57C8 into descriptor 2's +0x20 (0x0030B6D5-0x0030B6DC), and readers reach the bytes through that pointer. The load-time rebase zeroes all 512 bytes (0x0030B702-0x0030B737). This is the region the save payload field map lists as inventory class descriptors at payload +0x53C54, a genuine tenant of this block.

name: inventoryPackedFlags
meaning: 128 bytes in which only bits 0x1, 0x2 and 0x4 of each byte are derived state: the load-time rebase ands every byte with 0xF8, so bits 0x8 to 0x80 survive a load and are persisted. A reimplementation that zeroes this region destroys saved data. It ends at +0x5A48, exactly where the five slot maps begin.

name: slotMapClass0
meaning: One of five parallel slot maps, nine 2-byte entries each, 0x12 apart. Every reader takes the low byte of a 2-byte stride entry (movzx eax, byte [base + idx*2 + N]), so the upper byte of each entry is unread. The slot-map initialiser 0x00329CC0 fills map 0 and then copies it verbatim into the other four, so all five start identical. Class 0, and the only one the initialiser fills from the authored byte table at 0x01EED260.

name: pad5AA8

name: sequenceAccumFloat
meaning: The float part of an accumulator fed a per-frame delta by 0x00317230, which carries into +0x5ACC when it reaches the constant at 0x008F8180, the whole capped at 99,999,999 (0x5F5E0FF). 0x00320D50 reads it as int(+0x5AC8) + +0x5ACC; 0x00329E40(n) sets the integer part, and 0x00322200 and the block reset zero both. All five recorded accesses are float-class and not one is integer arithmetic, so it is typed float.

name: sequenceAccumInt
meaning: The integer part of the accumulator whose float part is +0x5AC8.

name: transitionFlags
meaning: Bit 0x1 gates a presentation branch; bit 0x2 is set by 0x00313600 and cleared by the command issuer 0x00311CF0's and mask. The save-transition restore is conditional on bit 0x2 of the captured copy: a record without it leaves this whole 16-byte block alone. Captured and restored as part of a 16-byte movups block, which is the move granularity and not the field: the conditional reads on the restore path show the internals.

name: pad5AD2

name: sequenceTimerB

name: transitionFlagsB

name: ladderState

name: pad5AF0

name: resultEchoA
meaning: Result echo A: the result-metadata apply 0x00385BA0 copies the result's +0x13C here when it is not -1 (0x00385BEA); 0x0038EBE0 subtracts it inside a per-mille computation (0x0038EC70); 0x00233C10 zeroes it on the restart path.

name: runtimeModeFlags
meaning: The battle runtime mode flag word. Bit 0x1 and bit 0x2 have their own accessors; it is also captured to and restored from the save transition record. The restore path also forces it: after replaying the two floats it sets bit 0x2 and clears bit 0x1, so a restored transition always lands in one specific mode regardless of what was captured.

name: dispatchedMode
meaning: The mode in effect as of the last dispatch, held by the party control mode transition dispatcher 0x0030D8B0 to drive the handler table at 0x01EECFC0. Read at 0x0030D8DB (movsxd rsi, dword [rdx+0x5b08]) and compared with the incoming mode in edi at 0x0030D90C. If it is unchanged, the dispatcher bounds-checks edi against 4 and calls the handler at [0x01EECFC0 + (r14 + edi*4)*8]. If it changed, it bounds-checks this field against 4 instead and calls [0x01EECFC0 + rsi*32 + (8 or 0x18)], the exit handler of the mode being left, before dispatching the new one. Either way 0x0030D97C then stores edi back into this field, under test ebp, ebp. Zeroed together with runtimeModeFlags (+0x5B04) by 0x0030DA10. Between dispatches the field holds the current mode; it is the previous mode only between the comparison and the write-back, so one variable serves for both.

name: resultEchoC

name: resultEchoB

meaning: the gambit configuration banks: three per party stats index, forty indices, 0x34 apart. Bank (i, b) is at +0x5B10 + (3*i + b) * 0x34, and which of the three is live comes from the selector array at +0x7370
